audience_description: Head of Department / Subject Leader (School) in Eduversal partner schools — an approved Level 5 school subject-leadership role that leads subject quality within one school. Reports to the Academic Coordinator / Vice Principal and the Principal according to the school structure; coordinates with the Eduversal Subject Specialist, other Heads of Department and relevant coordinators. Key accountabilities: curriculum implementation, assessment quality, department improvement, teacher support, data review, subject meetings, resource planning and follow-up of agreed actions (Career Growth: Framework 26-27 §10.2). Keeps the department's Department Handbook current (Curriculum Module: Department Handbook Template 26-27) and is one of the school's appraisers for formal F2 observations (Teacher Appraisal: Handbook 26-27).

framework_anchors.cambridge_teacher_standards_2023: Subject Leader is held to teacher standards plus the leadership tasks below.
framework_anchors.teacher_appraisal_handbook_26_27: Subject Leaders are appraised on F1-F4 plus F3L Leadership Responsibilities (six items), and are one of the school's appraisers: the school's appraisers formally observe each teacher in the Teacher Appraisal population at least three times per semester, recorded in Edunav Appraisal.
framework_anchors.department_handbook_template_26_27: The department's one operating handbook: profile, curriculum framework, assessment implementation, roles, meeting rhythm, evidence set, semester close-out.
framework_anchors.career_growth_framework_26_27: §10.2 role profile; §13 meeting rhythm (Principal – Heads of Department and department meetings every two weeks; inter-level department meetings quarterly).

priority_levels.compliance: Legally required, Cambridge-required, or a controlled minimum in a network document. Non-negotiable.

recurring_tasks.title: Plan and submit your own lessons on time
recurring_tasks.description: Subject Leaders teach and lead. Submit your own lesson plans by the school's deadline, using the Teaching & Learning: Lesson Planning Guide & Template 26-27.
evidence_required: Plans submitted in the school system
recurring_tasks.first_time_guide: You set the tone. If you submit late, your department will too.

recurring_tasks.title: Walkthroughs in your department (formative)
recurring_tasks.description: Make short snapshot visits to department classrooms and give written feedback on the Teacher Appraisal: Walkthrough Form 26-27, shared with the teacher in writing through Edunav. Walkthroughs are developmental: they carry no score and are never part of the F2 calculation.
recurring_tasks.first_time_guide: Keep walkthroughs and formal observations apart. A walkthrough is a short developmental visit; a formal F2 observation uses the level-specific rubric and is recorded in Edunav Appraisal.

recurring_tasks.title: Carry out your share of formal F2 observations
recurring_tasks.description: The school's appraisers — Subject Leader / Head of Department, Principal, Academic or Cambridge Coordinator — formally observe each teacher in the Teacher Appraisal population at least three times per semester. For each observation you lead: review the teacher's lesson plan first, use the F2 rubric for the teacher's current level, record it in Edunav Appraisal with the required evidence, and hold the post-observation conference using Glow / Grow / Go. Teachers still in Teacher Induction are not on the F2 schedule, and a former mentor does not carry the F2 observations of their own mentee.
framework_anchor: Teacher Appraisal: Handbook 26-27 — F2 Classroom Observation
recurring_tasks.first_time_guide: A valid F2 observation needs an authorised and conflict-free appraiser, the right level-specific rubric, and a complete record in Edunav. A high or low score is never a reason to remove a valid observation.

recurring_tasks.title: Review a sample of department lesson plans
recurring_tasks.description: Look at a rotating sample of your department's plans against the Lesson Planning Guide & Template 26-27. Judge the quality and coherence of the planning, not its length, and use what you see in your coaching conversations.
recurring_tasks.first_time_guide: The guide should support a professional conversation rather than become a compliance checklist.

recurring_tasks.title: Coaching touch inside an existing check-in
recurring_tasks.description: Use your weekly or fortnightly check-ins with department teachers for the capacity-building coaching touches: one agreed growth focus per actively supported teacher, at most two per semester. Try one strategy for 1-2 weeks, then decide together — keep, adapt or replace. No separate meeting is needed. Teachers still in Teacher Induction stay in the Induction pathway instead.
evidence_required: Short working note on the teacher's tracking sheet
framework_anchor: Teaching & Learning: Teacher Capacity Building Guide 26-27
recurring_tasks.first_time_guide: Coaching is not telling. Let the teacher read their own progress first; where your read and theirs differ, that gap is usually the most useful part of the conversation. Capacity building is developmental and separate from appraisal.

recurring_tasks.title: Department records current
recurring_tasks.description: Same as for any teacher — attendance, grades and communication current — plus the department: summative scores entered in the Edunav Gradebook within five working days, and department meeting actions up to date in the one action tracker.

fortnightly_tasks.title: Lead the department meeting
fortnightly_tasks.description: Departments meet at least every two weeks, with minutes and named actions — more often around assessment, moderation, subject selection, external examinations or major curriculum changes. Core agenda: previous actions; curriculum coverage; student learning; assessment and moderation (upcoming Teacher-Paced / Synchronized responsibilities, marking consistency, feedback quality, remedial follow-up); one concrete teaching practice; resources and safety; upcoming milestones; action close — owner, due date, evidence of completion.
evidence_required: Minutes with named actions, owners and due dates
framework_anchor: Department Handbook Template 26-27 — Department meeting rhythm
fortnightly_tasks.first_time_guide: Do not create meetings only to generate minutes. Meeting minutes with no date, no attendance list and no action items are the pattern the School Appraisal evidence guide flags.

fortnightly_tasks.title: Principal – Heads of Department meeting
fortnightly_tasks.description: Join the Principal's Heads of Department meeting, held every two weeks. Bring your department's performance, implementation progress, support needs and any unresolved academic risk that needs escalation; leave with agreed actions.

monthly_tasks.title: Review student work and move from scores to action
monthly_tasks.description: Sample student work across the department's classes. For each gap you find, name the learning objective or skill, agree targeted re-teaching or support, assign an owner and set a review point. Use the Assessment Policy for remedial rules — do not invent a parallel retake system.
evidence_required: Support actions recorded in the action tracker
framework_anchor: Department Handbook Template 26-27 — Student support and intervention
monthly_tasks.first_time_guide: Name-by-name discussion is fine for genuine intervention, but keep only the academic and support information you need.

termly_tasks.title: Department moderation and standardisation
termly_tasks.description: Hold a moderation meeting with the teachers of the same subject: review a sample of student work together, calibrate marking against the agreed criteria and rubrics, and use Cambridge exemplar material for IGCSE and A Level courses. For Common Assessment, the Academic Coordinator also samples 3-5 papers per school against the mark scheme before results are final.

termly_tasks.title: Cambridge syllabus updates and examiner reports (if Cambridge subject)
termly_tasks.description: Review Cambridge's syllabus update notices with the Principal or Academic Coordinator and make sure the changes are in the Scheme of Work. After each results release, use the subject-level results report and the examiner reports to adjust the Scheme of Work where they show a curriculum gap.
termly_tasks.applies_when: subject is Cambridge IGCSE / AS-A / Checkpoint

termly_tasks.title: Capacity-building progress conversations
termly_tasks.description: Hold a short progress conversation with each teacher you are supporting: read progress together, then decide whether to continue or shift the focus. In the same week the Principal or Academic Coordinator reviews the pattern with all Subject Leaders — report in phrases, not case by case. At year end this becomes the full review conversation.

termly_tasks.title: Resource, safety and resource-map check
termly_tasks.description: At least once per semester, check that teachers have what they need to deliver the planned curriculum: availability, condition, access, replacement needs, storage and safe use — not just whether an item is on the inventory. Review your subject resource map at the same time and remove dead links and low-value tools. Science departments use the Science & Laboratory Handbook 26-27; digital tools follow Digital Citizenship & AI requirements.
framework_anchor: Department Handbook Template 26-27 — Resource and safety readiness

termly_tasks.title: Inter-level department meeting
termly_tasks.description: Meet with the same department at the other school levels for curriculum continuity, transition, resource sharing and cross-level collaboration.

1.focus: Department Handbook current, Scheme of Work confirmed, coaching focus agreed

tasks.title: Update the Department Handbook and hold the first department meeting
tasks.description: Update the Department Handbook for the new year — department roles, curriculum and assessment references pointing to current sources, meeting rhythm and action tracking, student-support and resource responsibilities, links to the live evidence. Remove any superseded assessment term, old appraisal rule or legacy weighting. Walk the department through it at the first meeting.
tasks.first_time_guide: The handbook records how the department carries out approved rules; it does not rewrite them. It must not create local grading weights, new EASE rules, unofficial appraisal criteria or alternative exam requirements.

tasks.title: Confirm the Scheme of Work and coverage tracker
tasks.description: Confirm the Scheme of Work / scope and sequence and the coverage tracker for each year group, following the Annual Plan in Edunav. Use the Cambridge Curriculum Learning Objectives spreadsheet as a mapping reference; current official syllabi remain authoritative. Raise any gap between the Cambridge and national requirements with the Academic Coordinator rather than resolving it alone.
evidence_required: Scheme of Work and coverage tracker linked in the Department Handbook

tasks.title: Capacity-building kickoff conversations
tasks.description: With each teacher you will support this semester, agree one growth focus together (at most two), using the diagnosis as a starting point, not a verdict.

2.focus: Colleague and mentor for each new teacher

tasks.title: Help the Principal match each new teacher with a mentor
tasks.description: If your department has new teachers, help the Principal find an eligible mentor for each one: a mentor must hold an active Mentor Certification and support no more than 3 mentees. The Principal assigns the colleague and the mentor, and the teacher, mentor and school leader sign the Induction Agreement.
evidence_required: Mentor named in the Induction Agreement

3.focus: Formal observation schedule; subject results analysis

tasks.title: Plan this semester's formal observations with the Academic Coordinator
tasks.description: Agree which appraiser observes which teacher so that every teacher in the Teacher Appraisal population gets at least three valid formal observations this semester, each by an authorised and conflict-free appraiser.

tasks.title: Analyse the May/June Cambridge results for your subject
tasks.description: Use the subject-level report from the Exams Officer: grade distributions, component performance, predicted against actual grades and trends. Agree what changes in the Scheme of Work and in teaching.

tasks.title: EASE Week 1 — lessons continue
tasks.description: EASE Week 1 is mid-semester: EASE Growth runs for Grades 7-12 and normal lessons continue. Teacher-Paced Tests may also fall this week, inside the class's regular period, following the Annual Plan. EASE Growth is never a department grade and is not entered in the Gradebook.

14.week_label: EASE Week 2 — Semester I Synchronized Test

tasks.title: Lead your subject through the Semester I Synchronized Test
tasks.description: EASE Week 2: normal lessons stop for the network testing block. The Synchronized Test is online only, through Latihan.id. Make sure department teachers know their supervision and marking duties: manually graded questions are marked with the M1 / A1 / B1 mark scheme, and all results are entered in Edunav. Where the live EASE Schedule replaces the Synchronized Test with a Cambridge exam for a grade or subject, follow the schedule.

tasks.title: Lead end-of-Semester I moderation for the department
tasks.description: Review marking of the semester's summative work together and resolve differences against the agreed criteria before results are final.

tasks.title: Give the Exams Officer your subject's candidates and tiers (if Cambridge subject)
tasks.description: Subject selection happens the term before entries. Recommend each candidate's subject and tier (for example Extended or Core) to the Principal or Academic Coordinator, who approve the combination; the Exams Officer records the approved list. Review predicted grades with the Principal before anything is submitted.

tasks.title: Record the Semester I close-out in the Department Handbook
tasks.description: Record: major coverage completed and any carry-forward gaps; assessment and moderation lessons; priority student-support actions; teaching practices worth keeping; resource gaps and requests; one to three Semester II priorities.
evidence_required: Semester I review in the Department Handbook

tasks.title: Agree the Semester II coaching focus
tasks.description: Where a teacher's focus now reads 'Now Consistent', introduce the second priority; otherwise continue the same focus into Semester II.

tasks.title: Analyse the October/November Cambridge results for your subject
tasks.description: Use the subject-level report from the Exams Officer and the examiner reports: grade distributions, component performance, predicted against actual grades. Update the Scheme of Work where the examiner report shows a curriculum gap.

tasks.title: EASE Week 3 — lessons continue
tasks.description: EASE Week 3 is mid-semester: EASE Growth runs for Grades 7-12 (exam-heavy grades may sit earlier) and normal lessons continue. Teacher-Paced Tests may also fall this week, inside the regular period, following the Annual Plan.

33.week_label: EASE Week 4 — Semester II Synchronized Test

tasks.title: Lead your subject through the Semester II Synchronized Test
tasks.description: EASE Week 4: normal lessons stop. Same routine as EASE Week 2 — online through Latihan.id, M1 / A1 / B1 marking for manually graded questions, results entered in Edunav, and the live EASE Schedule decides where a Cambridge exam replaces the Synchronized Test.

tasks.title: Give the Exams Officer your subject's candidates and tiers (if Cambridge subject)
tasks.description: Subject selection happens the term before entries. Recommend each October/November candidate's subject and tier to the Principal or Academic Coordinator, who approve the combination; the Exams Officer records the approved list. Standard October/November entries close before September.

tasks.title: Lead end-of-Semester II moderation
tasks.description: Review marking of the semester's summative work together and resolve differences against the agreed criteria before results are final.

tasks.title: Check each teacher's appraisal record is complete
tasks.description: For the teachers whose appraisal you lead, check the record in Edunav: at least three valid formal observations per semester (or a documented exception agreed by school management with Eduversal), and both Student Survey results. Remind teachers to bring their F3 evidence to the End-of-Year Conference.
framework_anchor: Teacher Appraisal: Handbook 26-27 — Full Appraisal Cycle

tasks.title: Hold the End-of-Year Conferences you lead
tasks.description: The teacher presents their evidence; you score F3 only after that. The composite is calculated only when all applicable frameworks are complete. Use Glow / Grow / Go, agree objectives for next year, and write the appraisal statement in Edunav.

tasks.title: Turn the year's review into next year's priorities
tasks.description: Convert the semester close-outs into a small number of next-year priorities, not a long wish list, and update the Department Handbook. If you are handing the department to a new Subject Leader, walk them through the handbook, open actions in the tracker, carry-forward coverage gaps and student-support actions in progress.
evidence_required: Next-year priorities in the Department Handbook
framework_anchor: Department Handbook Template 26-27 — Semester close-out and handover

extra_tasks_first_12_weeks.title: Handover walk-through and early transition review
extra_tasks_first_12_weeks.description: In your first weeks, have the outgoing Subject Leader (or, if they are not available, the Academic Coordinator) walk you through the Department Handbook, open actions, coverage gaps and student-support actions. Later, hold an early transition review with the Academic Coordinator or Principal.

extra_tasks_first_12_weeks.title: Mentor Certification before you mentor
extra_tasks_first_12_weeks.description: If you will mentor a new teacher, you must hold an active Mentor Certification before you are assigned.

writes_to: Department meeting minutes and action tracker
feeds_into: Teacher Appraisal F2 (formal observations recorded in Edunav) and F3L (own appraisal)
School Appraisal D3-B evidence (department meeting minutes and actions)
